On-disk cache of fetched dataset payloads.
doc.description: Entries live under ``$XDG_CACHE_HOME/xrayatlas`` (default ``~/.cache/xrayatlas``). Each entry is a data file plus a metadata file holding the key and the SHA-256 of the data. A read verifies both; an entry that fails verification is deleted and reads as a miss. Writes are atomic (temporary file then rename), data first and metadata second, so an interrupted write is never mistaken for a valid entry. Concurrent processes are not locked, so the worst case under contention is a temporary miss, never a corrupt hit. The cache never stores tokens.

Compare optical models by aligned peaks and normalized-channel differences.
doc.description: Pure local computation over already-fetched `Model` objects. The only network access is `Model.normalized`, which is computed by the server; this module never normalizes, fits, or interpolates. Peaks group under the single-linkage rule described in `Comparison.peaks`, and spectra align on exact keys, holding ``NaN`` wherever a model lacks a value.

classes.name: Comparison

doc.summary: Peaks and normalized channels of several models on shared, aligned axes.
doc.description: Create with `compare`; the models and tolerance are fixed at construction, and `spectra` is safe to call more than once. Direct construction validates the same tolerance and requires one unique label per model that is not already a frame column name: ``center_ev``, ``count``, ``energy_ev``, ``theta_deg``, and ``phi_deg`` are reserved, and a label must not equal another model's derived ``{label}_minus_{first_label}`` column. Omit ``labels`` to derive ``tag#version`` labels.

sections.name: Raises
sections.text:
ValidationError: ``models`` is empty or holds a non-`Model` entry, ``labels`` is not one
    unique string per model or collides with a frame column name, or ``tolerance_ev`` is
    not a positive finite number of eV.

entries.name: ValidationError
entries.description: ``models`` is empty or holds a non-`Model` entry, ``labels`` is not one unique string per model or collides with a frame column name, or ``tolerance_ev`` is not a positive finite number of eV.

classes.signature: Comparison(models: Sequence[Model], labels: Sequence[str] | None = None, tolerance_ev: float = 0.2)

doc.summary: One row per aligned peak group, sorted by group center ascending.
doc.description: Centers chain into one group while each next center is at most the tolerance past the group's widest center. Each model contributes at most one peak per group: the one nearest the group's mean center, ties to the lower center. Columns are `center_ev` (mean of the contributing peaks), `count` (how many models contributed), then one center column per model labeled ``tag#version`` (``tag#draft`` for an unpublished version). A model with no peak in a group holds ``NaN``. Repeated labels gain a ``#2``, ``#3``, ... suffix (``tag#1#2`` for a second read of ``tag#1``). No peaks at all still yields those columns with zero rows. The frame is a copy: editing it does not change later reads.

entries.name: dataset
entries.description: A `Dataset`, an Atlas id, or a UUID passed through to `Model.normalized` (server-side normalization; never recomputed here). ``None`` lets each model use its single linked dataset.

sections.name: Returns
sections.text:
A DataFrame holding, in order: the alignment keys (`theta_deg`, `phi_deg`, and
`energy_ev`; the geometry keys only when at least one frame has a finite ``theta_deg``
or ``phi_deg`` value, energy alone otherwise), one channel column per model label as
in `peaks`, then one ``{label}_minus_{first_label}`` difference column for every model
after the first. Rows sort by the keys exactly like `Dataset.spectra` (missing
geometry last). A key one model lacks holds ``NaN`` in that model's column, and
difference columns never use filled or interpolated values: a model whose geometry
labels differ from every other model's yields an all-``NaN`` difference column rather
than a cross-geometry subtraction. Energy grids must agree exactly: two dataset
versions whose sample energies differ even in the last bit produce disjoint rows and
``NaN`` differences instead of a resampled comparison.

sections.name: Raises
sections.text:
ValidationError: ``channel`` is not one of the supported channels; a model reports a
    non-numeric key or channel value; or one model reports two rows at the same key.
    The key is the ordered geometry pair plus the energy, so one model must not hold
    two rows for the same geometry and energy (``polarization_id`` is not part of it).

entries.name: ValidationError
entries.description: ``channel`` is not one of the supported channels; a model reports a non-numeric key or channel value; or one model reports two rows at the same key. The key is the ordered geometry pair plus the energy, so one model must not hold two rows for the same geometry and energy (``polarization_id`` is not part of it).

classes.signature: TensorHandle(client: Client, tag: str, version: VersionSelector, sha256: str, byte_size: int, manifest: TensorManifest | None)

doc.summary: Download (or read from the cache) and return the tensor array.
doc.description: Every call first resolves a fresh signed URL from the server (one small request); the cache avoids only re-downloading the tensor blob itself, so ``load`` still needs the network. The blob bytes are verified against the SHA-256 and size the server reports on every read, and the array is checked against the stored manifest when one exists, so a corrupt or swapped cache entry is evicted and repaired rather than served. The dtype is whatever the publisher stored, ``float64`` or ``complex128``. Read the result as named parameter columns, not as a physical tensor: axis 1 follows the manifest ``components``, and a complex payload holds delta in its real part and beta in its imaginary part as a storage convenience. The archive is loaded without pickle support.

sections.text:
AtlasError: The digest or size does not match, the array does not match its manifest
    shape or dtype, the archive has no ``tensor`` array, or the stored format is not
    ``npz``.

doc.summary: Building, publishing, sharing, and reviewing optical models.
doc.description: `model()` returns a `ModelBuilder` context manager: it reads the source model on enter and writes only on a clean exit (fork, then draft, then tensor); publishing is always a separate explicit call. doc.summary: Stored optical-model parameter payloads.
doc.description: A `Tensor` is built from the user's own array with `Tensor.from_array`, which validates it, writes a compressed ``.npz`` (arrays ``tensor`` and ``energy_ev``), computes its SHA-256, and builds the manifest the server stores. The client never computes optical constants. Does no network I/O. The stored object is a container for named parameter columns, not a physical tensor: axis 1 is labelled by `TENSOR_COMPONENTS`, and the values a researcher works with today are the optical constants ``delta`` and ``beta`` (or directional columns such as ``xx``) as separate series on a shared energy axis. A complex array is a storage convenience for carrying delta in the real part and beta in the imaginary part; the client stores complex arrays as ``complex128`` (widening ``complex64`` exactly) and floats as ``float64``, and it never narrows complex data to a real dtype. A real tensor with coordinate transforms and physical invariants is future work, so do not read the array shape as one.

doc.summary: Validate named parameter columns and serialize them.
doc.description: The dtype policy is lossless: ``float16``, ``float32``, ``float64``, ``complex64``, and ``complex128`` are accepted. ``float16`` and ``float32`` widen to ``float64`` and ``complex64`` widens to ``complex128`` (exact, no precision loss) before serializing, so the stored dtype is always ``float64`` or ``complex128``. Integer, boolean, object, and string dtypes are rejected so a silently widened or coerced tensor cannot hide a mistake; an integer array must be cast explicitly by the caller.

doc.summary: Typed models of optical model content and server responses.
doc.description: Fields are snake_case in Python and camelCase on the wire. Request-side models (``_Req``) are strict: they reject unknown fields, reject wrong Python types (for example a string or a bool where a number is expected), and enforce the same limits as the server (finite numbers, ordered windows, size caps, UUID identifiers) so mistakes fail before any HTTP call. Response-side models (``_Wire``) ignore unknown fields so older clients keep working. Server responses are parsed with ``parse_model(cls, data, strict=False)``, which relaxes type coercion for that call only. Use `xrayatlas.validate.parse_model` to turn a pydantic failure into `ValidationError`. This module does no I/O.

Windows are in eV, each requires ``low < high``, and each pre window must end at or before its post window starts. doc.summary: Client-side validation helpers.
doc.description: Turns pydantic failures into `ValidationError` with the offending field path, and converts a peak table (a pandas DataFrame) into validated `Peak` objects. Does no I/O.

functions.name: parse_model
functions.signature: parse_model(cls: type[ModelT], data: dict[str, Any], *, strict: bool = True) -> ModelT

doc.summary: Build ``cls`` from ``data`` or raise `ValidationError` naming each failing field.
doc.description: Request models are parsed strictly by default: wrong Python types (a string where a number is expected, a list where a tuple is expected) and unknown keys are errors. Pass ``strict=False`` only when parsing a server response, so that JSON-decoded lists coerce to tuples and numeric strings are accepted; the response models in `xrayatlas.types` still reject non-finite values.

sections.name: Args
sections.text:
cls: A pydantic model class from `xrayatlas.types`.
data: Field values, snake_case or camelCase.
strict: ``True`` (the default) for request input; ``False`` for server responses.

entries.name: data
entries.description: Field values, snake_case or camelCase.

entries.name: strict
entries.description: ``True`` (the default) for request input; ``False`` for server responses.

sections.text: The validated model.

sections.text: ValidationError: One or more fields failed; the message lists ``path: reason`` lines.

functions.signature: is_finite_number(value: object) -> bool

doc.summary: Whether ``value`` is a finite int or float (booleans are not numbers).

functions.name: clean_tag
functions.signature: clean_tag(tag: str) -> str

doc.summary: Normalize a model tag, or raise `ValidationError`.
doc.description: Strips surrounding whitespace, lowercases, drops one leading ``m/`` or ``/``, and requires eight lowercase ASCII letters or digits. The Atlas mints base32-style tags (its alphabet omits ``i``, ``l``, ``o``, ``u``), but the client accepts any eight lowercase alphanumerics so tests and future generators keep working; the server's own schema is laxer (1 to 32 characters). Typical valid tags: ``k7m2xq4n``, ``newmodel``.

sections.name: Returns
sections.text: The cleaned tag.

sections.name: Raises
sections.text: ValidationError: The cleaned tag is not eight lowercase ASCII letters or digits.

entries.name: ValidationError
entries.description: The cleaned tag is not eight lowercase ASCII letters or digits.

functions.name: validate_peaks
functions.signature: validate_peaks(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[Peak]

doc.summary: Convert a peak table into validated peaks.
doc.description: Columns: ``center_ev`` (required, eV), and optionally ``kind``, ``transition``, ``amplitude``, ``width``, ``shape``, ``center_err``, ``amplitude_err``, ``width_err``, ``dataset`` (experiment UUID string), ``polarization`` (polarization UUID string), and the fit provenance columns ``fit_tool`` with ``fit_version`` and ``fit_code_hash`` (which require ``fit_tool``); these map to each peak's ``fit_provenance``. Every other column is folded into each peak's ``params`` (strings, finite numbers, or booleans). A missing value (NaN or None) in an optional column means "not set"; infinity anywhere, a boolean in a numeric column, or a missing or non-finite ``center_ev`` is an error. Row order becomes peak order. An empty table (no rows, with a ``center_ev`` column) returns ``[]``.

sections.name: Args
sections.text: df: The peak table. Columns must be flat and unique.

entries.name: df
entries.description: The peak table. Columns must be flat and unique.

sections.name: Returns
sections.text: One `Peak` per row.

sections.name: Raises
sections.text:
ValidationError: ``df`` is not a DataFrame, has MultiIndex or duplicate column names, lacks
    a ``center_ev`` column (the message suggests near matches), has more than 2000 rows, or
    holds an invalid value; the message names the row and column.

entries.name: ValidationError
entries.description: ``df`` is not a DataFrame, has MultiIndex or duplicate column names, lacks a ``center_ev`` column (the message suggests near matches), has more than 2000 rows, or holds an invalid value; the message names the row and column.
